label: Velocity Kinematics and Statics
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 171 through 218 and turns forward kinematics into its differential shadow. We ask one guiding question across every slide: what does the Jacobian reveal about instantaneous motion, directions the arm cannot move, and the static force balance that the same matrix transpose silently governs.

label: From Pose to Rate
notes: Forward kinematics gives a configuration map from joint angles to end-effector pose. Differentiating that map in time produces velocity kinematics, a linear relation valid only at the current configuration. The Jacobian is the slope of this nonlinear map, recomputed afresh at every posture the manipulator visits.

label: The Manipulator Jacobian
notes: The Jacobian assembles partial derivatives of the configuration map into a matrix that sends joint-rate vectors to an end-effector twist. Each column is the twist generated by moving one joint alone at unit rate while every other joint is frozen, so columns carry direct physical meaning.

label: The Space Jacobian
notes: The space Jacobian expresses the end-effector twist in the fixed base frame. Its columns are joint screw axes pushed forward through the product of exponentials up to that joint, so each column is the instantaneous screw the joint contributes as seen by an observer standing in the world frame.

label: The Body Jacobian
notes: The body Jacobian expresses the same twist in the end-effector frame. Its columns are joint screw axes pulled back from the tip, and the body and space Jacobians are related by the adjoint of the end-effector pose, two coordinate views of one underlying linear map between rates and motion.

label: Columns Are Screw Axes
notes: Reading the Jacobian column by column makes geometry visible. Each column is a six-vector with angular and linear parts, the screw axis of one joint expressed in the chosen frame. The span of these columns is exactly the set of twists the manipulator can produce at this instant from its joints.

label: Kinematic Singularities
notes: A singularity is a configuration where the Jacobian loses rank, so its columns become linearly dependent. The arm instantaneously cannot generate motion in some twist direction, no matter how the joints move. Singularities are rank events tied to geometry, not numerical accidents, and they bound the usable workspace.

label: The Manipulability Ellipsoid
notes: Mapping the unit sphere of joint velocities through the Jacobian yields an ellipsoid of achievable end-effector twists. Its axis directions are eigenvectors of J J transpose and its semi-axis lengths are singular values, so a long, round ellipsoid means dexterity and a flat one warns of an approaching singularity.

label: Dexterity Measures
notes: Scalar summaries of the ellipsoid quantify dexterity. The product of singular values, proportional to the ellipsoid volume, vanishes exactly at singularities. The condition number, the ratio of largest to smallest singular value, blows up there. These numbers let a planner steer the arm away from poorly conditioned postures.

label: Statics and Virtual Work
notes: Hold the arm still and let it resist an external wrench at the tip. The principle of virtual work equates joint power with end-effector power for any virtual displacement, and because this holds for every joint rate the wrench and torque relation must hold as a matrix identity independent of motion.

label: Force from the Transpose
notes: Virtual work forces the joint torques that balance a tip wrench to equal the Jacobian transpose times that wrench. The same matrix that maps rates to twists maps forces backward to torques. This kineto-statics duality means velocity and force live in dual spaces joined by one transpose.

label: Force Ellipsoid and Duality
notes: At a singularity the velocity ellipsoid flattens, but the force ellipsoid, governed by the inverse Jacobian transpose, stretches along the same lost direction. The arm cannot move there yet resists force effortlessly. Directions of easy motion and directions of easy force are reciprocal throughout the workspace.

label: Recap and Invariants
notes: We unified instantaneous motion and static force through one matrix. The Jacobian maps joint rates to twists, its rank loss marks singularities, its singular values shape the manipulability ellipsoid, and its transpose converts tip wrenches into joint torques. The notebook checks an invariant power pairing to guard against frame and adjoint mistakes.
